title: SPECTRAL DETECTOR -- tells whether a sound is pitched, noisy or silent

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Menu: choose Live Input (mic/line input 1) or File Player.
File Player: drop a sound file into the player and press play.
The big label shows the result: PITCH, NOISE or SILENT. The number beside it is 2 / 1 / 0.
Pitchedness bar: how periodic the sound is, from 0 (noise) to 1 (clean pitch).
Threshold: how pitched a sound must be to count as PITCH (0.5-0.95).
Smooth ms: how long the result must hold before it flips (50-1000 ms).
Floor dB: input level below which the sound counts as SILENT (-80 to -10 dB).
Monitor: listen to the selected source. It starts silent.

sections.heading: INPUTS & OUTPUTS
lines: The state (0 silent, 1 noise, 2 pitch) is sent to [receive detector-state] for other patches.
It is only sent when the state changes.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: A gen~ codebox high-passes the input at 70 Hz and runs an autocorrelation over 80 Hz-2 kHz.
The best correlation peak is the raw pitchedness, then it is smoothed.
A hysteresis band stops the result chattering near the threshold.
The silence gate uses the loudest of RMS, peak and a boosted high-frequency peak.
